title: Property, power, and infrastructure glossary
description: Look up terms used in property records, commercial insurance, lending, site selection, and grid studies. Each definition links to the formula, source record, or workflow behind it.

examples.label: Find the tax lot attached to an address
examples.detail: San Francisco’s Main Library is on parcel 0354001. Keep the leading zero and store the jurisdiction with the number.

examples.label: Check which buildings are on an insurance schedule
examples.detail: Appanoose County’s 2021 schedule used eight building IDs and 12 coverage rows at one address. Reconcile by building and coverage.

examples.label: Compare loan payments with property income
examples.detail: A property with $600,000 in annual net operating income and $480,000 in annual debt payments has 1.25× coverage.

examples.label: Evaluate a data center connection under a grid outage
examples.detail: In the two-line study example, the proposed 60 MW fits in normal operation. The limiting outage leaves room for only 35 MW.

examples.label: Calculate overlap between two stores
examples.detail: In the Detroit example, the share of Whittier’s catchment also reached by Micah’s rose from 17.2% at 15 minutes to 42.5% at 20 minutes.

examples.label: Compare a feeder’s load and export records
examples.detail: National Grid published both 0.10 MW of solar export hosting capacity and 3.18 MVA of summer load headroom for one Vail Mills feeder.

examples.label: Read the combined generator testing limit
examples.detail: The Harwood draft proposes one rolling 3,039 engine-hour testing cap for 192 generators. Check the signed permit and each engine’s separate rules.
